terms.label: Processing has a journalistic purpose
terms.definition: The controller's CMS records classify the processing as journalism.

anchors.clause_title: § 4 Processing of personal data for journalistic purposes
anchors.quote: Personal data may be processed and disclosed in the media for journalistic purposes without the consent of the data subject, in particular disclosed in the media, if there is public interest and this is in accordance with the principles of journalism ethics.
anchors.note: Journalistic-purpose gateway to the consent-free processing basis.

terms.label: There is public interest in the processing
terms.definition: Editorial assessment confirms that there is public interest in the processing.

anchors.clause_title: § 4 Processing of personal data for journalistic purposes

anchors.note: Public-interest condition for the journalism basis.

terms.label: Processing respects journalism ethics
terms.definition: The editorial team confirms the processing is consistent with journalism ethics.

terms.label: Data subject has consented
terms.definition: Consent records show the data subject has given valid consent.

anchors.quote: Personal data may be processed and disclosed in the media for journalistic purposes without the consent of the data subject ...
anchors.note: Consent baseline: when consent exists, the journalism basis is not needed.

terms.label: Disclosure would cause excessive damage to the data subject's rights
terms.definition: Editorial risk assessment concludes that disclosure would cause excessive damage to the data subject's rights (§ 4, second sentence).

anchors.quote: Disclosure of personal data must not cause excessive damage to the rights of any data subjects.
anchors.note: Proportionality limit: excessive harm defeats the journalism basis.
